   **English:** MS 1 has: “He placed [it]; and from then on he was called Charles, king of the Franks and Lan…”; after this, a line and a half has been erased, followed by *Tuncque ad hoc*, “And then for this purpose.” MS 1b and the edition have the abbreviated continuation *p. et tam ipse r. q. et u. m. e. id se i. c. b. P. et e. v. sacramento—fratribus commendavit*. In context: “[he placed it], and both the king himself and all his magnates [pledged] by oath to blessed Peter and his vicars that they would preserve it forever … he commended himself to the brethren.” The initials are retained because the note gives only an abbreviated form of the passage.

98. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] ita 1c. c. eidem papae t. 1b.]`

   **English:** MS 1c has the printed wording *se inperpetuum conservaturos beato Petro et ejus vicariis*, “[pledging] to blessed Peter and his vicars that they would preserve it forever.” MS 1b instead has abbreviated *c. eidem papae t.*, “… to the same pope …”; the surrounding initials are not expanded in the note. *Ita* is the editor’s “thus,” identifying MS 1c’s agreement, not a word attributed to that manuscript.

99. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] Postmodum vero praefatus rex una c. P. f. Beneventum perrexit cum m. e. super 1b. ed.]`

   **English:** MS 1b and the edition read *Postmodum vero praefatus rex una c. P. f. Beneventum perrexit cum m. e. super*: “Afterwards, however, the aforesaid king, together with Pippin his son, went to Benevento with a great army against [Arichis].” The abbreviated names and army phrase are supplied by the adjacent narrative.

100. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] quem supra jam memoravimus add. 1b. ed.]`

   **English:** MS 1b and the edition add *quem supra jam memoravimus*, “whom we have already mentioned above,” after Arichis.

101. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] fuit 1b.]`

   **English:** MS 1b reads perfect *fuit* instead of imperfect *erat*, both “was,” in the statement that Arichis was King Desiderius’s son-in-law.

102. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] ita 1c. rex 1b.]`

   **English:** MS 1c has the printed name *Carolus*, “Charles”; MS 1b instead reads *rex*, “the king.” Here *ita* means “thus [as printed]” and is not itself a manuscript reading.

103. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] d. artatus Arichis, et c. suam, et m. p. t. n. et g. s. G. s. (scilicet deest 1b) et A. eidem Carolo obsides p. g. tradidit. Hinc Francorum 1b. ed.]`

   **English:** MS 1b and the edition have the abbreviated alternative *d. artatus Arichis, et c. suam, et m. p. t. n. et g. s. G. s. … et A. eidem Carolo obsides p. g. tradidit. Hinc Francorum*: “At last Arichis, hard pressed, handed over his crown, the greater part of his treasure, and his two children, namely Grimoald and Adelgisa, to that same Charles as hostages for peace. Hence [fear] of the Franks ….” MS 1b omits *scilicet*, “namely,” not the word for the children. The initials correspond to the fuller adjacent narrative.

104. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507C] Id jam apud Erch. non legitur.]`

   **English:** “This is no longer read in Erchempert.” The note is attached to the statement that Charles received Arichis’s crown.

105. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507C] c. n. B. a. non habet Erch.]`

   **English:** Erchempert does not have *civitatem novam Benevento addidit*, “he added a new city to Benevento,” abbreviated in the source note as *c. n. B. a.*

106. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507C] Pesto.]`

   **English:** The editor identifies the place called *Lucania* here as Pesto, Paestum.

107. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507C] Nocera de' Pagani.]`

   **English:** The editor identifies Nuceria as Nocera de’ Pagani.

108. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507C] Eadem in Chr. Vult. p. 359 leguntur, ex relatione Petri presb. qua noster quoque usus esse videtur.]`

   **English:** “The same account is read in the *Chronicle of the Volturno*, p. 359, from the report of the priest Peter, which our author also seems to have used.”

109. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] degentibus ac D. 1. ed.]`

   **English:** MS 1 and the edition read *degentibus ac D.* for *Deo*: with the following words, “the brethren dwelling here and serving God.” The main text has simply “the brethren serving God here.”

110. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] Tuncque ab hoc primum rege praefatus abbas praeceptum conf. de t. terra S. B. (t. hac terra ed.) recepit. Alio etiam p. praedictus rex sancto B. c. (c. s. B. ed.) mon. 1. ed.]`

   **English:** MS 1 and the edition read the abbreviated account: “Then the aforesaid abbot first received from this king a charter of confirmation concerning all the land of Saint Benedict.” The edition instead has *t. hac terra*, “all this land.” It continues *Alio etiam p. praedictus rex sancto B. c. (c. s. B. ed.) mon.*: “By another charter also the aforesaid king confirmed to Saint Benedict the monastery …,” with the edition placing “confirmed” before “to Saint Benedict.” The surviving abbreviations are retained rather than completed with an invented list of properties.

111. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507C] Gatt. Acc. p. 13 e Reg. Petri D cf. p. 111 Böhmer Reg. Kar. 128. Suspectum redditur verbis [Col. 0508C] in cod. subscriptis: Carolus g. D. imperator augustus.]`

   **English:** Gattola, *Accessiones*, p. 13, from Peter the Deacon’s Register; compare p. 111 and Böhmer, *Regesta Karolorum*, no. 128. “It is rendered suspect by the words subscribed in the manuscript: ‘Charles, by the grace of God emperor Augustus.’”

112. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0508C] ib. p. 14.]`

   **English:** “In the same work, p. 14”: Gattola, *Accessiones*, referring to the second charter.

113. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] et s. M. i. P. add. 1b.]`

   **English:** MS 1b adds *et s. M. i. P.*, “and Saint Mary in Plumbariola,” the church named in the adjacent text.

114. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] necnon---junctae add. 1b.]`

   **English:** MS 1b adds the entire clause from *necnon* through *junctae*: “and also all the waters, with the banks on both sides, wherever they adjoined the lands of this monastery.”

115. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0508C] Tosti I. p. 98. e Petri Neg. Data XVIII Kal. Martii. Anno 30 regni nostri. Ind. VII. Actum civitate Papia.]`

   **English:** Tosti, volume I, p. 98, from Peter’s Register (the supplied note has *Neg.*): “Dated the eighteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the thirtieth year of our reign, indiction VII. Executed in the city of Pavia.” The Roman date is preserved; it is not 18 February.

116. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] deest 1b.]`

   **English:** MS 1b omits *hujus*, “this,” from *terris hujus monasterii*, “the lands of this monastery.”

117. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] deest ed.]`

   **English:** The edition omits *et*, “also,” after *Sed* in “But he also gave authority.”

118. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0508C] In praecepto illo de S. M. in Cingla, etc. ut quae de ripis addidit noster, alieno loco inseruisse videatur: quod plus semel fecit.]`

   **English:** “In that charter concerning Saint Mary in Cingla, etc.; thus our author seems to have inserted what he added about the riverbanks in the wrong place—a thing he did more than once.”

119. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] m. sibi (i. t. s. r. add. 1b.) absque a. p. s. v. abbatem eligerent 1.]`

   **English:** MS 1 reads *m. sibi … absque a. p. s. v. abbatem eligerent*: “the monks should elect an abbot for themselves without anyone’s prejudice or violence.” MS 1b adds abbreviated *i. t. s. r.*, “according to the tenor of the holy Rule,” corresponding to the fuller adjacent text.

120. **Source:** `[Note: [Col. 0507] Ad hunc idem Karolus per Adelgarium (del in loco raso) (ep. add. 1b.) litteras misit 1. Ad hunc abbatem idem K. per Aldegarium (Adelg. 3.) ep. litt. a Francia dest. ed. Aldegarium 4.]`

   **English:** MS 1 reads: “To this [abbot] the same Charles sent letters through Adelgarius,” with *del* in the name written on an erasure; MS 1b adds *ep.*, “bishop.” The edition reads: “To this abbot the same Charles sent letters from France through Bishop Aldegarius”; MS 3 has *Adelg.* instead of *Aldegarium*, while MS 4 has *Aldegarium*. These variants stand at the transition beginning *Reversus*, “Having returned.”

The abbreviated readings concern the brethren requested from the monastery; *ad* belongs to the printed readings, not to the witness numbers.

123. **[Col. 0507]** `s. c. desunt` — “seu constituendam” (“or to establish”) is omitted in witness 1 and in the edition.

139. **[Col. 0509]** `et par.` — “and likewise” (the edition).

154. **[Col. 0509]** `foce` — “mouth/estuary” (witnesses 1 and 2).

156. **[Col. 0509]** `Per idem tempus (an. 782. Apr.) Hildeprandus quoque Spoletii dux obtulit in hoc monasterio curtem quae dicitur Castrinianum cum omnibus pertinentiis ejus in comitatu Pinnensi; et olivetum in Tronto, loco qui vocatur Turri. In comitatu vero Marsorum, loco qui Paternus appellatur, curtem quingentorum simul modiorum; et familias multas cum omnibus substantiis earum; nec non et aliquot piscatores in lacu Fucino cum portu ejusdem lacus vocabulo Adrestina. Insuper et gualdum suum nomine Cusanum` — “At the same time (April 782), Hildeprandus, duke of Spoleto, also offered to this monastery the estate called Castrinianum, with all its dependencies, in the county of Pinna; and an olive grove at Tronto, in a place called Turri. In the county of the Marsi, in a place called Paternus, an estate of five hundred modii together; and many households with all their possessions; and also some fishermen on Lake Fucino with its harbor, called Adrestina. Moreover, his woodland called Cusanum.” The entire span from `Per` through `Cusanum` is added in witness 1b.

157. **[Col. 0510C]** In the ninth year of Charles’s reign in Italy, the ninth year of Hildeprand’s duchy, indiction 5; Gattola, *Accessiones*, p. 18, from Peter’s Register.

158. **[Col. 0509]** `Hildebr.` — “Hildebrand” (witness 1b and the edition).

159. **[Col. 0510C]** Pinna is now called Civita di Penna, in Further Abruzzo.

160. **[Col. 0509]** `dicitur` — “is called” (witness 1b and the edition).

161. **[Col. 0509]** `vocatur` — “is called” (witness 1b and the edition).

166. **[Col. 0509]** `Guacco` is corrected to `Wacco` in witness 1b; `Vacco` appears in witness 4. These are variant spellings of the personal name Wacco/Vacco, not different persons.

167. MS 1b omits *constitutus*, “stationed/engaged”, after *in expeditione*, “on campaign”.

168. **[Col. 0510C]** “The charter of this offering does not survive.”

169. **[Col. 0509]** `filiolum` — “little son” (reading 3).

171. **[Col. 0509]** `casale et aliud` — “a rural estate and another” (the edition, consistently).

172. **[Col. 0509]** `casale et aliud` — “a rural estate and another” (the edition, consistently).

181. **[Col. 0511]** `atque consiliarius` — “and counsellor” is added in witness 1.

182. **[Col. 0511]** `ipsius` — “of that same person/thing” (witness 1 and the edition).

185. **[Col. 0511]** `Varn.` — “Varn.” (witness 4); the abbreviated name is retained as printed.

186. **[Col. 0511]** `Teodelenda` — “Teodelenda” (witness 3), a variant spelling of the personal name.

188. **[Col. 0511]** `ac` — “and” (witness 4).

189. **[Col. 0511]** `esset` — “was/would be” is added in witness 1b and the edition.

190. MS 1 and the edition read *p. accusatus e. r. fuisset a q. invidis, q.*, “after he had been accused before that king by certain envious men, that …”, placing the accusation before the reference to the king.

200. **[Col. 0511]** `illi: ut eruantur inquiunt ejus oculi, ne` — “to him: ‘Let his eyes be removed,’ they say, ‘lest …’” (reading 1); `illi: Jubete inq. ut er. ejus oc. ne` — “to him: ‘Command, they say, that his eyes be removed, lest …’” (reading 2).

201. MS 1 and the edition have *d. Et ubi vel q. ait rex t.*, “[send …]. And where or when, said the king, [shall we find] so …”, placing *vel quando*, “or when”, before the speech attribution. MS 1b inserts *vel q.*, “or when”, above the line. The source abbreviates the boundary words.

202. MS 1 and the edition read *v. videntes c. i. regis compassionem ac ben.*, “but seeing the king’s compassion and goodwill toward him”, for the wording about considering the kindly king’s goodwill.
